post.summary:
Queues making the database as a new file: format sqlite, postgres or sqlserver (a script), bak or dump (native).
202, then M:GrifballWebApp.Server.DatabaseBackup.BackupController.DownloadStatus(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken) follows it and M:GrifballWebApp.Server.DatabaseBackup.BackupController.Download(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken) hands it over: a large one takes
longer than a proxy waits for a response. 400 for another format; 409 while another backup or export is queued or
runs; 409 when there's no server here to make that native backup on (the message says why).

get.summary: The format's backup (one kept a format): being made, made, or failed; and the format being made now, whichever. 400 for another format.

The format's backup M:GrifballWebApp.Server.DatabaseBackup.BackupController.StartDownload(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken) made, once it's made; 404 when there's none (not made, or discarded since). 400 for another format.

post.summary:
Queues copying the database into a new one (missing, or without tables) on the given server: 202, then
M:GrifballWebApp.Server.DatabaseBackup.BackupController.ExportStatus(System.Threading.CancellationToken) follows it. 409 while a backup or export is queued or runs; 400 for an unknown
provider or a connection string it can't read. The connection string is used for this export only: never kept
or logged, and the job it's handed to gets it protected (readable for an hour).

schema.description: Where to export the database: SqlServer, Postgres or Sqlite, and the new database's connection string.

post.summary:
Signs in with a password. A browser gets the session cookie (GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.BrowserAuth.CookieName) and an
empty 200. With useCookies false the answer is a bearer token instead
(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.BearerToken.AccessTokenResponse), for clients that are not browsers.
Creates a new account with a username and password, in the Player role.

get.summary:
Leaves for Discord's sign-in, which comes back to the login page (`/login?callback=true`), and that
page calls M:GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.IdentityController.ExternalLoginCallback(System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken). followUp, the page to go on to, is kept
only if it is a path on this site (M:GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.IdentityController.IsAppRelativePath(System.String)), escaped as one query value.

post.summary:
Finishes a Discord sign-in: the session cookie, or with useCookies false a bearer token.
Discord sign-in and the bot know a player by the same Discord id: a first sign-in joins the account the bot already
links to that id, and an account made or signed in here gets that link (GrifballWebApp.Application.Identity.IDiscordAccountLinkService).
A POST, as it creates the user and signs in: the browser comes back from Discord to the login page (a page
of the app, not this action), which then calls this with the antiforgery token like any other change.
A new bearer token for a refresh token (bearer clients only; browsers have the cookie).

get.summary: Who is signed in: their display name, user ID and roles.

Who is signed in, for the client (in the browser, and on the server while it renders a page with the
visitor's cookie): M:GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.IdentityController.MetaInfo, or 204 No Content for a visitor. Unlike MetaInfo, a visitor is
not an error, so the client asks on every first load without logging a failed request.

The antiforgery request token, which the browser sends in GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.BrowserAuth.AntiforgeryHeader with
every change (GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.CookieAntiforgeryFilter). Also sets the antiforgery cookie it pairs with. The
token belongs to the user signed in when it was made, so the client asks again after signing in or out.

post.summary: Signs the current browser session out.
post.description:
Clears the session cookie (and any half-finished Discord sign-in). No antiforgery token needed: signing
someone out is all a forged request could do, and SameSite=Lax already keeps the cookie off cross-site POSTs.
Also changes the user's security stamp, so a copy of the cookie (and the user's other sessions) stops working
within GrifballWebApp.Server.Identity.BrowserAuth.SecurityStampValidationInterval.

post.summary: Sets a new password using a one-time reset token.

BackupInfoDto.description: What the Database Backup page shows: the server the app is on, the migration a backup is at, and the formats it can download.

ClientLogDto.description: A log line, in the trace it names (if any).

kind.description: `internal` (a navigation) or `client` (a call to the API).

ClientSpanDto.description: A finished span. Times are the browser's clock, in epoch milliseconds.

ClientTelemetryBatchDto.description: One batch from a browser: what it collected since its last. Every list and text is bounded.

ClientVitalDto.description: One Web Vital: web-vitals' value, milliseconds (CLS unitless).

ExportRequestDto.description: Where to export the database: SqlServer, Postgres or Sqlite, and the new database's connection string.

HaloAuthCodeRequest.description: A Microsoft OAuth code for the site's Halo account (Direct mode).

HaloStatusDto.description:
What the Infinite Client page shows (`Admin/HaloStatus`). Direct mode: only GrifballWebApp.Server.HaloInfinite.HaloStatusDto.Mode; the page then
asks `Admin/CheckStatus` as it always has. Gateway mode: the gateway's address and admin page, whether this
environment has an API key for it (never the key), and a fresh probe: whether the gateway answered at all
(GrifballWebApp.Server.HaloInfinite.HaloStatusDto.Reachable), its Halo account's status word (GrifballWebApp.Server.HaloInfinite.HaloStatusDto.AccountStatus, from its `/health`) and
what the test call through it answered (GrifballWebApp.Server.HaloInfinite.HaloStatusDto.ApiCode).

JobIntervalRequest.description: A job's new interval, in seconds.

JobPausedRequest.description: Whether a job's schedule is paused.

providers.description: The external providers this server is configured for. Filled in by the controller.

LogsDto.description: Newest first. Truncated: the limit was reached, older lines were left out.

MetricSeriesDto.description: A point: Unix milliseconds and the value.

count.description: How many players are in the queue.

open.description:
Matchmaking runs here, so joining is allowed: not in a preview without Discord, where the matchmaking tick is off
and nobody who joined would ever be matched.

hasGamertag.description: The user has a gamertag linked, which joining needs.

QueueStatusDto.description: The matchmaking queue as the signed-in user (if any) sees it.

RescheduleRequestedDto.description: A reschedule request made: its ID.

SetGamertagRequest.description: A gamertag to set on one's own profile.

SpanDto.description: A span: OffsetMs from the trace's first span. Status is Unset, Ok or Error.

TelemetryStatusDto.description: Which parts of the Telemetry page have a backend (TelemetryQuery:*), and the service.name they are scoped to.

TraceDto.description: This service's spans of a trace, in start order.
